agentic.summary: Reviewed conversation (turns 0-29) using provided excerpts. No personal data, verification, promises, or conduct violations found. One minor escalation violation: the customer expressed complaint/asked for help and the agent did not offer escalation (supervisor/complaint form/internal team).

findings.quote: Sorry. I have no way of getting to the package. It is in the hands of the delivery service and they are already en route.
findings.explanation: The customer expressed a complaint and asked if anything could be done in turns 24-26. Per policy, when a customer makes a complaint the agent must acknowledge it and offer an escalation route (supervisor, complaint form, or internal team). Although the agent acknowledged the situation, they did not offer any escalation option or next steps.

full.summary: Minor issues: agent attempted an order action before the account was pulled (verification) and made an over-confident delivery timing claim (promises). No personal/payment data, escalation, or conduct violations found.

findings.quote: You're welcome! Let's proceed with the overnight shipping update.
findings.explanation: The agent says they will proceed with an order change before the system shows the account was pulled (system log at turn 12). Policy requires pulling up the account before any account or order action; doing so after announcing an action is a verification lapse.

findings.quote: The shipping cannot be changed if in transit. But, in transit means you will get either today or tomorrow at the latest.
findings.explanation: The agent makes a definitive-sounding delivery timing claim ('you will get either today or tomorrow at the latest'), which is over-confident. The policy flags over-confident guarantees about likely outcomes as a minor violation.

rag.summary: Audit of provided excerpts: one escalation violation (agent failed to offer escalation when customer complained). No violations in personal_data, verification, promises, or conduct.
